definition_zh: 博士的；博士学位的；博士研究的
definition_en: relating to a doctorate, the highest university degree, or to the research and students connected with it
core_image: 一顶博士帽压在一摞改过无数遍的论文上
scene: 答辩室的灯亮到深夜，桌上摊着改得密密麻麻的稿子。She finally finished her doctoral dissertation after six years of fieldwork.
sceneCN: 这里 doctoral 是「博士研究的」（第 2 个义项：与博士论文和博士研究有关）；句意是她做了六年田野调查后终于完成了博士论文。

pos.zh: 形容词：博士的；博士学位的；博士研究的

derivatives.zh: 由 doctor 加名词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「博士学位」
由前缀 post-「之后」加 doctoral 构成，义为「博士后的」

senses.title: Relating to a doctorate
senses.definition: relating to the highest university degree, which is awarded after original research
senses.definitionCN: 与最高一级大学学位有关的，该学位须在原创研究之后授予
senses.example: A doctoral degree usually takes at least three years.
senses.exampleCN: 博士学位通常至少需要三年。
senses.why: Latin doctor meant teacher, and the suffix -al turns that title into an adjective of belonging, so the degree is named after the teacher it certifies.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 doctor 是「教师」，后缀 -al 把这个称号变成表示归属的形容词；这个学位正是以它所要认证的教师身份来命名的。

senses.title: Relating to dissertation research
senses.definition: connected with the original research and dissertation required for a doctorate
senses.definitionCN: 与取得博士学位所需的原创研究和学位论文有关的
senses.example: Her doctoral work examined how coastal soils change over time.
senses.exampleCN: 她的博士研究工作考察了沿海土壤随时间发生的变化。
senses.why: Research is the substance of the degree, so the same adjective naturally describes the long investigation behind the thesis.
senses.whyCN: 研究是这一学位的实质内容，因此同一个形容词自然也能描述论文背后那场漫长的调查。

senses.title: Relating to a doctoral candidate
senses.definition: used to describe a student who is working toward a doctorate
senses.definitionCN: 用来描述正在攻读博士学位的学生
senses.example: Doctoral candidates must defend their findings before a committee.
senses.exampleCN: 博士生必须在委员会面前为自己的研究成果答辩。
senses.why: The person is named after the degree still being earned, so one adjective covers both the title and the reader for it.
senses.whyCN: 人是以尚未到手的学位来命名的，所以同一个形容词既能修饰学位，也能修饰正在攻读它的人。

intro.en: Doctoral is built on Latin doctor, a teacher, plus the English adjective suffix -al.
intro.cn: doctoral 由拉丁语 doctor（教师）加英语形容词后缀 -al 构成。

items.en: The teaching verb behind Latin docere is usually traced to a root meaning to take or accept; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 docere 背后的「教」义一般追溯到表示「拿取、接受」的词根，更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Docere meant to teach or to show, and it also produced doctrina, teaching, and doctor.
items.cn: docere 意为「教、示范」，它还生出 doctrina（教导）与 doctor。

items.en: Doctor was an agent noun meaning teacher, and in the universities it became a title for a learned master.
items.cn: doctor 是施事名词，意为「教师」；在大学里逐渐成为博学之士的头衔。

items.en: Doctoratus named the degree of a doctor; the earliest university records are from the thirteenth century, though exact dates are uncertain.
items.cn: doctoratus 指博士的学位；最早的大学记录出现在十三世纪，确切年代仍有争议。

items.en: English formed doctoral from doctor plus -al to describe anything belonging to the degree.
items.cn: 英语用 doctor 加 -al 造出 doctoral，用来描述属于这一学位的事物。

items.en: The adjective spread from degrees to dissertations, research projects and candidates.
items.cn: 这个形容词从学位扩展到论文、研究项目以及在读的候选人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin teaching root; the near-meaning group gathers other academic labels.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「教」这个词根；近义组收的是其他学术称谓。

entries.definition: A person holding the highest university degree, or a medical practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指拥有最高大学学位的人，也指医生；与 doctoral 同出拉丁语 docere。

entries.definition: The degree itself, formed from doctor with the noun suffix -ate.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「博士学位」，由 doctor 加名词后缀 -ate 构成。

entries.definition: Describing research done after a doctorate has been awarded.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「博士后的」，指取得博士学位之后所做的研究。

entries.definition: A student or course above the first degree level; broader than doctoral.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「研究生、研究生的」，范围比 doctoral 更宽。

entries.definition: Relating to universities and scholarly study in general.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「学术的、大学的」，泛指高校与学术研究。

entries.definition: Showing careful academic study and knowledge; it describes style, not a degree.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有学者风范的、博学的」，描述风格而非学位层级。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real Latin family of docere, to teach, and show where each form fits.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的拉丁词族 docere（教）展开，并说明每个形式的位置。

normal.en: Docere means to teach; every word in this family starts from a classroom.
normal.cn: docere 意为「教」，这一族的每个词都从课堂出发。

normal.en: Doctor was first a teacher, then a learned title, and only later a medical doctor.
normal.cn: doctor 先是教师，后来成为博学头衔，最后才常指医生。

normal.en: Doctorate is the degree, so doctoral describes what belongs to that degree.
normal.cn: doctorate 是学位本身，doctoral 则描述属于这个学位的事物。

normal.en: The suffix -al simply means relating to, as in doctoral research.
normal.cn: 后缀 -al 只表示「与……有关」，如 doctoral research 中的用法。

normal.en: Post- means after, so postdoctoral work begins once the degree is in hand.
normal.cn: post- 表示「之后」，所以 postdoctoral 指拿到学位之后的研究。

abstract.en: Picture a square cap resting on a tower of corrected pages.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶方形博士帽压在一摞改过无数遍的纸页上。

abstract.en: Picture a long table where one candidate answers questions late into the night.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，一位候选人在灯下答辩到深夜。

abstract.en: Picture the word doctor written on a doorplate, with al added like a name tag.
abstract.cn: 想象门牌上写着 doctor，再贴上一枚 al 的名牌。

examples.en: She is writing her doctoral thesis on ancient soils.
examples.cn: 她正在写关于古代土壤的博士论文。

examples.en: The laboratory offers places for doctoral students from abroad.
examples.cn: 这个实验室为来自海外的博士生提供名额。

examples.en: His doctoral research was published as a short book.
examples.cn: 他的博士研究被出版成了一本小书。

dict_mnemonic.text: doctor 是「博士」，加上 -al 就成了「博士的」；doctoral 修饰学位、研究和在读的学生。

root: 由拉丁语 docere（教、示范）派生：docere 生出 doctor（教师）与 doctrina（教导），中世纪拉丁语 doctoratus 指博士学位，英语再以 doctor 加 -al 构成 doctoral。更早的印欧词根一般追溯到表示「拿取、接受」的形式，更深的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: One adjective covers the degree, the research behind it and the person still working for it.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个形容词覆盖了学位本身、支撑学位的论文研究，以及仍在攻读的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a square cap placed on a tall pile of revised pages.
core.cn: 核心意象：一顶方形博士帽放在一摞改过多遍的纸页上。

branches.en: THE DEGREE: doctoral names what belongs to the doctorate itself.
branches.cn: 学位线：doctoral 指属于博士学位本身的事物。

branches.en: THE WORK: the adjective also names the research and dissertation that earn the degree.
branches.cn: 研究线：这个形容词也指为取得学位而做的研究与论文。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a candidate carries the adjective of the degree still being earned.
branches.cn: 人物线：在读的候选人带着那个尚未到手的学位的形容词。

branches.en: Degree and research share one label because the degree is defined by the research.
branches.cn: 学位与研究共用一个标签，因为学位正是由研究来定义的。

branches.en: The same word describes the thesis and the person writing it.
branches.cn: 同一个词既能描述论文，也能描述写论文的人。

intro.en: Doctoral joins a Latin teaching root to an ordinary English adjective suffix.
intro.cn: doctoral 把拉丁语「教」的词根接到一个普通的英语形容词后缀上。

latinIntro.en: Latin docere, doctor and doctrina are recorded; doctoratus belongs to medieval university Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 docere、doctor 与 doctrina 均有文献记录；doctoratus 属中世纪大学拉丁语。

items.example: The verb is the teaching root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的「教」词根。

items.example: The title first meant a learned teacher.
items.exampleCN: 这个头衔最初指博学的教师。

items.example: She earned her doctorate at thirty.
items.exampleCN: 她三十岁取得了博士学位。

items.example: The doctoral programme lasts four years.
items.exampleCN: 这个博士项目持续四年。

items.example: It turns doctor into doctoral.
items.exampleCN: 它把 doctor 变成 doctoral。

items.example: It forms doctorate.
It forms postdoctoral.
The noun shares the same teaching root.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词共享同一个「教」词根。

latinEntries.meaning: the rank or degree of a doctor

definition_zh: 文件；公文；证件；记录，用文件证明；电子文档
definition_en: a written, printed or electronic record that gives information or proof, or to record something in a permanent form
core_image: 一叠盖章的纸，把发生过的事固定下来
scene: 移民官把一摞材料推到窗口前，逐页翻看。Please bring every document needed for the visa interview.
sceneCN: 这里 document 是「文件、材料」（第 1 个义项：提供信息或证据的书面记录）；句意是请带上签证面谈所需的全部文件。

pos.zh: 名词：文件；公文；证件；电子文档
动词：记录；用文件证明

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「文件记录；证明材料」
由本词加后缀 -ary 构成，义为「纪录片；文件的、纪实的」
由否定前缀 un- 加过去分词构成，义为「无证件的；无记录的」

senses.title: A written record
senses.definition: a piece of written, printed or electronic matter that provides information or evidence
senses.definitionCN: 提供信息或证据的书面、印刷或电子材料
senses.example: The historian found a document describing the old harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家找到了一份描述旧港口的文件。
senses.why: Latin documentum was a lesson or a proof, something that teaches because it shows the facts.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 documentum 是「教训、凭证」，它之所以能教人，是因为把事实摆了出来。

senses.title: An official paper
senses.definition: an official paper such as a passport, certificate or contract that proves identity, rights or an agreement
senses.definitionCN: 护照、证书或合同等官方纸张，用来证明身份、权利或协议
senses.example: No one may enter the site without the proper documents.
senses.exampleCN: 没有正式证件，任何人不得进入该场地。
senses.why: When a record carries a stamp or a signature, it stops being private notes and becomes proof that others must accept.
senses.whyCN: 当一份记录盖上印章或签上名字，它就不再是私人笔记，而成了别人必须承认的凭证。

senses.title: To record something
senses.definition: to record an event, a process or a fact in writing, photographs or another lasting form
senses.definitionCN: 用文字、照片或其他持久形式记录事件、过程或事实
senses.example: The team documented every step of the experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 团队记录了实验的每一个步骤。
senses.why: The noun turns into an action: facts are fixed on paper so that later readers can check them.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动作：把事实固定在纸上，好让后来的人可以核对。

senses.title: A computer file
senses.definition: a file created by a word processor or similar program, containing text and often images
senses.definitionCN: 由文字处理软件或类似程序创建、含文字并常含图片的文件
senses.example: Save the document before you close the programme.
senses.exampleCN: 关闭程序前请先保存这份文档。
senses.why: The paper record moved onto a screen, but the name stayed because the purpose is the same: a fixed body of text to return to.
senses.whyCN: 纸张上的记录搬到了屏幕上，但名称留了下来，因为用途没变：一份可以反复调取的固定文本。

intro.en: Document goes back to Latin documentum, a lesson or a proof, built on docere, to teach.
intro.cn: document 可追溯到拉丁语 documentum（教训、凭证），其根是 docere（教）。

items.en: Docere meant to teach or to show, and it produced doctor and doctrina as well.
items.cn: docere 意为「教、显示」，它还生出 doctor 与 doctrina。

items.en: Documentum meant a lesson, a warning or a piece of evidence, something that shows what is true.
items.cn: documentum 指教训、警示或证据，也就是能把真相摆出来的东西。

items.en: Old French document carried the legal and written senses into Middle English.
items.cn: 古法语 document 把法律与书面义带入中古英语。

items.en: The noun is recorded in English from the fourteenth century, first for an authoritative written record.
items.cn: 英语中这个名词自十四世纪有记录，最初指有权威性的书面记录。

items.en: The verb to document, meaning to support with evidence, became common in travel and science writing.
items.cn: 动词 document 表示「以证据支持」，在游记与科学写作中逐渐常见。

items.en: The computer age added the electronic file to the family without changing the core idea of a fixed record.
items.cn: 计算机时代把电子文件加进这一族，却没有改变「固定记录」的核心意思。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the Latin doc root; the near-meaning group gathers other kinds of written proof.
note.cn: 形近组守着拉丁语 doc 词根；近义组收的是其他种类的书面凭证。

entries.definition: Written material that records or supports something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「文件记录、证明材料」，与本词共享 doc 词根。

entries.definition: A factual film or programme, or an adjective meaning based on records.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指「纪录片」，形容词指「纪实的、文件的」，同出本词。

entries.definition: A holder of the highest degree or a medical practitioner; it shares docere, to teach.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指博士或医生；与 document 同出拉丁语 docere（教）。

entries.definition: A collection of papers or data kept together under one name.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「档案、文件」，指归在同一名下的纸张或数据。

entries.definition: A written or stored account of facts; broader and less formal than document.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「记录」，范围为广、正式程度低于 document。

entries.definition: An official paper that proves a fact, such as a birth or a qualification.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「证书」，指证明出生、资格等事实的官方纸张。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real docere family and the everyday places documents appear.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用真实的 docere 词族，以及文件实际出现的日常场景。

normal.en: Docere is to teach: a document teaches later readers what happened.
normal.cn: docere 是「教」：一份文件教后来的人知道发生过什么。

normal.en: Doctor, doctrine and document all come from the same teaching root.
normal.cn: doctor、doctrine 与 document 都出自同一个「教」的词根。

normal.en: A travel document is a passport or visa, not a diary.
normal.cn: travel document 指护照或签证，不是日记。

normal.en: The verb document appears in phrases such as document the process.
normal.cn: 动词 document 常见于 document the process 这类搭配。

normal.en: An electronic document keeps the old name because it is still a fixed text.
normal.cn: 电子文档沿用旧名，因为它仍然是固定下来的文本。

abstract.en: Picture a folder whose pages are pinned down by a heavy stamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一个文件夹，纸页被一枚沉重的印章压住。

abstract.en: Picture a camera beside a notebook, both recording the same event.
abstract.cn: 想象相机和笔记本并排放着，记录同一件事。

abstract.en: Picture a paper page sliding into a screen without losing its edges.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸滑进屏幕里，却没有失去自己的边界。

examples.en: Every claim in the report must be supported by a document.
examples.cn: 报告中的每一项说法都必须有文件支持。

examples.en: They documented the damage with photographs and measurements.
examples.cn: 他们用照片和测量数据记录了受损情况。

examples.en: She opened the document and began to edit the first paragraph.
examples.cn: 她打开文档，开始修改第一段。

dict_mnemonic.text: doc 有「教、示」的意思，-ment 是名词后缀：把事实摆出来教给别人看，就是一份文件。

root: 源自拉丁语 documentum（教训、证据、范例），由 docere（教、显示）加名词后缀 -mentum 构成；docere 同时生出 doctor 与 doctrina。古法语 document 把书面与法律义带入英语，动词用法在十八世纪普及。

sensesIntro.en: From a written record to an official proof, an act of recording, and finally a file on a screen.
sensesIntro.cn: 从书面记录，到官方凭证，再到记录这一动作，最后落到屏幕上的电子文件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of stamped pages that pins down what happened.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠盖了章的纸页，把发生过的事固定住。

branches.en: THE RECORD: written matter that carries information from one reader to the next.
branches.cn: 记录线：把信息从一位读者传给下一位读者的书面材料。

branches.en: THE STAMP: official marks turn a record into proof of identity or rights.
branches.cn: 印章线：官方标记把记录变成身份或权利的证明。

branches.en: THE ACT: the verb names the work of fixing facts in a lasting form.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词指把事实固定成持久形式的工作。

branches.en: THE SCREEN: the same fixed text now lives in a computer file.
branches.cn: 屏幕线：同一份固定文本如今住在电脑文件里。

branches.en: Private notes and official papers share one word because both preserve what was said.
branches.cn: 私人笔记与官方文书共用一个词，因为两者都保存了所说过的话。

intro.en: Document is a Latin noun whose suffix -mentum names a result; English adds further suffixes for its family.
intro.cn: document 是拉丁语名词，后缀 -mentum 表示结果；英语再用其他后缀扩展这一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin docere, documentum and doctrina are all recorded, so only the deeper root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 docere、documentum 与 doctrina 均有记录，只有更早的词根属于重构。

items.example: The root verb means to show the facts.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根动词表示把事实摆出来。

items.example: The Latin noun already meant a piece of evidence.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词本义就是一件证据。

items.meaning: result or means of an action
items.example: It carries the result sense of documentum.
items.exampleCN: 它承接了 documentum 表示结果的含义。

items.example: The film is documentary in style.
items.exampleCN: 这部影片是纪实风格的。

items.meaning: the act or body of recording
items.example: Good documentation saves time later.
items.exampleCN: 良好的记录能省下以后的时间。

items.example: The outbreak is well documented.
Many workers remain undocumented.
items.exampleCN: 许多工人仍没有正式证件。

items.example: It forms documentary.

definition_en: a domesticated animal kept as a pet or for work, a male of this animal, or to follow someone closely
core_image: 雨夜门口的一双湿爪子，和一双怎样都不肯离开的眼睛
scene: 院门口传来爪子刨土的声音，屋里的灯忽然亮了。The dog barked at every passing car until midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 dog 是「狗」（第 1 个义项：被人饲养的家犬）；句意是那只狗对着每一辆经过的车叫，一直叫到半夜。

pos.zh: 名词：狗；公狗；雄兽
动词：尾随；纠缠

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「顽强的、不屈不挠的」
由本词加 -y 构成，义为「小狗；狗的，像狗的」
由 watch 加 dog 构成的复合词，义为「看门狗；监督者」

senses.title: A domesticated canine
senses.definition: a common domestic animal with four legs, kept as a pet, for guarding or for working
senses.definitionCN: 一种常见的四足家养动物，可作宠物、看门或工作用
senses.example: Their dog sleeps at the foot of the bed.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的狗睡在床脚边。
senses.why: The word first named a specific kind of dog in Old English, and the general sense grew from that one familiar animal at the door.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在古英语里先指某一类狗，后来从门口那只最熟悉的动物扩大成通称。

senses.title: A male canine
senses.definition: an adult male dog, or a male of other animals such as foxes
senses.definitionCN: 成年的公狗，也指狐狸等其他动物的雄性
senses.example: The litter had three dogs and two bitches.
senses.exampleCN: 这一窝里有三只公狗和两只母狗。
senses.why: Farm and hunting speech needed a plain word for the male, and dog took that role beside bitch.
senses.whyCN: 农事与狩猎用语需要一个直白的词来指雄性，dog 便与 bitch 相对承担了这个角色。

senses.title: To follow persistently
senses.definition: to follow someone closely and keep troubling them, as a dog follows a scent
senses.definitionCN: 像狗循着气味一样紧跟某人，并不断纠缠
senses.example: Reporters dogged the minister for weeks after the leak.
senses.exampleCN: 泄密之后，记者缠着那位部长追问了好几周。
senses.why: The animal's habit of following a trail turned into a verb for trouble that will not let a person go.
senses.whyCN: 这种动物循迹而行的习性变成了动词，用来形容一种不肯放过某人的麻烦。

intro.en: Dog is an Old English word of uncertain origin; it replaced the older general word hound in everyday use.
intro.cn: dog 是古英语词，来源不确定；它在日常用语中取代了更早的通称 hound。

items.en: Docga is recorded as a name for a kind of dog, but its earlier history is source uncertain.
items.cn: docga 有记录，指某一类狗，但它更早的历史来源不确定。

items.en: Dogge spread as the everyday word, while hound narrowed to hunting dogs.
items.cn: dogge 作为日常词扩散，hound 则缩小为猎犬。

items.en: The verb sense to follow closely appears, drawn from a dog trailing a scent.
items.cn: 「紧跟」的动词义出现，来自狗循着气味追踪的画面。

items.en: Dog days, the hot weeks of summer, was borrowed from the dog star Sirius.
items.cn: dog days 指夏季最热的几周，借自天狼星这一「狗星」的说法。

items.en: Dog now covers pets, working animals and figurative uses such as watchdog.
items.cn: 今天 dog 覆盖宠物、工作犬，以及 watchdog 这类比喻用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dog stem and its compounds; the near-meaning group names other canines.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dog 词干及其复合词；近义组收的是其他犬类称呼。

entries.definition: Determined and unwilling to give up, formed from dog plus -ed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「顽强的、不屈不挠的」，由本词加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: A child's word for a dog, or an adjective meaning dog-like.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指「小狗」，也可作形容词表示「狗的、像狗的」。

entries.definition: A fixed belief laid down by an authority; it only looks similar and comes from Greek.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「教条、信条」；只是拼写相近，词源来自希腊语，与 dog 无关。

entries.definition: A hunting dog, or to chase someone relentlessly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指「猎犬」，动词指「追逼」，是 dog 的较老同义词。

entries.definition: A young dog.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「幼犬、小狗」。

entries.definition: A dog or a tooth shaped like a dog's; a formal or scientific term.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「犬、犬齿、犬的」，属正式或科学用语。

normalIntro.en: These hooks stay with the real animal and the words English actually builds from it.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子守住真实的动物，以及英语实际由它构成的词。

normal.en: Dog replaced the older word hound in ordinary speech.
normal.cn: dog 在日常言谈中取代了更早的 hound。

normal.en: Dog days are named after the dog star, not after panting pets.
normal.cn: dog days 得名于天狼星这颗「狗星」，并非因为狗在喘气。

normal.en: A watchdog guards a gate; the compound adds a job to the animal.
normal.cn: watchdog 守在门口，复合词给这种动物加上了一项职责。

normal.en: The verb dog means to trail someone as a dog trails a scent.
normal.cn: 动词 dog 指像狗循着气味一样尾随某人。

normal.en: Dogged, from the same stem, means stubborn rather than dog-like.
normal.cn: 同词干的 dogged 表示顽强，而不是「像狗」。

abstract.en: Picture a wet nose pressed against a closed door, refusing to leave.
abstract.cn: 想象一只湿鼻子贴在紧闭的门上，怎样都不肯离开。

abstract.en: Picture a reporter walking behind a minister at exactly the same pace.
abstract.cn: 想象一名记者以完全相同的步速跟在部长身后。

abstract.en: Picture a small shadow at the edge of a fire, waiting for one word.
abstract.cn: 想象火堆边的一道小影子，等着一句呼唤。

examples.en: A dog waited by the gate every afternoon.
examples.cn: 每天下午都有一只狗守在门边。

examples.en: The dogged reporter would not drop the story.
examples.cn: 那位顽强的记者不肯放弃这条报道。

examples.en: Questions dogged the committee until the vote was held.
examples.cn: 质疑一直缠着委员会，直到投票举行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「多格」——门口那只大狗趴在格子地砖上，谁经过都要叫两声。

root: dog 来自古英语 docga，具体所指最初只是某一类狗，更早的来源不确定，也不能可靠地拆出词根。中古英语 dogge 逐渐取代 hound 成为通称；动词「尾随」义来自狗循迹追踪的习性。

sensesIntro.en: One animal name gives a general pet, a word for the male, and a verb for trouble that follows you.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个动物名称，既给出家犬通称，也给出指雄性的词，还长出「紧追不放」的动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wet paw at the door and eyes that will not look away.
core.cn: 核心意象：门口一只湿爪子，和一双不肯移开的眼睛。

branches.en: THE PET: the general name for a familiar domestic animal.
branches.cn: 宠物线：对一种熟悉家养动物的通称。

branches.en: THE MALE: a plain farm word for the male, paired with bitch.
branches.cn: 雄性线：农事用语里直指雄性的词，与 bitch 相对。

branches.en: THE PURSUIT: the animal's trailing habit becomes a verb for persistent trouble.
branches.cn: 追逐线：动物循迹的习性变成表示持续纠缠的动词。

branches.en: The pet and the pursuer are the same animal seen at rest and on a scent.
branches.cn: 宠物与追踪者是同一只动物，只是一个歇着，一个循着气味。

branches.en: Everyday speech uses the same word for the species and for the male.
branches.cn: 日常言谈用同一个词既指整个物种，也指雄性。

intro.en: Dog has no Latin root; English builds its small family with suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: dog 没有拉丁词根，英语用后缀与复合来搭出它的小词族。

latinIntro.en: There is no recorded Latin cognate of dog, so no Latin entries are listed here.
latinIntro.cn: dog 没有可考的拉丁同族词，因此这里不列拉丁条目。

items.example: Docga is the earliest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: docga 是最早有记录的形式。

items.meaning: the animal, or to follow closely
items.example: A dog guards the yard.
Two dogs slept outside.
Her dogged patience paid off.
items.exampleCN: 她那股顽强的耐心终于有了回报。

items.example: The press kept dogging the team.
items.exampleCN: 媒体一直缠着这支队伍。

items.example: The child called it a doggy.

items.meaning: a guard dog or a monitor
items.example: The agency acts as a watchdog.
He built a wooden doghouse.

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「顽强的、不屈不挠的」
由本词加 -y 构成，义为「小狗；狗的，像狗的」
由 watch 加 dog 构成的复合词，义为「看门狗；监督者」

definition_zh: 美元；一元（纸币或硬币）；元（其他英语国家的货币单位）
definition_en: the unit of money used in the United States and several other countries, or one unit of it in coins or notes
core_image: 一张被反复摊平的纸币，边角已经起了毛
scene: 收银台前，老人把皱巴巴的纸币一张张摊平。He paid three dollars for a small loaf of bread.
sceneCN: 这里 dollar 是「元」这一货币单位（第 2 个义项：以纸币或硬币形式出现的一元）；句意是他花三美元买了一个小面包。

pos.zh: 名词：美元；一元；元（其他英语国家的货币单位）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ization 构成，义为「美元化」，指一国改用美元作流通货币
由 petro-「石油」加本词构成，义为「石油美元」
由本词加 -ize 构成，义为「使美元化」

senses.title: The US unit of money
senses.definition: the standard unit of money in the United States, equal to one hundred cents
senses.definitionCN: 美国的标准货币单位，等于一百美分
senses.example: The dollar rose against the yen last week.
senses.exampleCN: 上周美元对日元升值。
senses.why: A silver coin from a Bohemian valley gave its name to a large coin, and that name travelled with trade to America.
senses.whyCN: 波希米亚一处山谷出产的银币把名字给了大银元，这个名字又随贸易传到美洲。

senses.title: One unit in coin or note
senses.definition: a coin or note worth one unit of this money
senses.definitionCN: 面值一元的硬币或纸币
senses.example: She found a dollar under the sofa cushion.
senses.exampleCN: 她在沙发垫下找到了一美元。
senses.why: The abstract unit becomes something you can hold, fold and hand across a counter.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的单位变成了能拿在手里、能折叠、能递过柜台的东西。

senses.title: The unit of other countries
senses.titleCN: 元（其他国家的货币单位）
senses.definition: the basic unit of money in several other countries, such as Canada, Australia and New Zealand
senses.definitionCN: 加拿大、澳大利亚、新西兰等若干国家的基本货币单位
senses.example: The ticket costs twenty Australian dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 这张票要二十澳元。
senses.why: Trade and empire carried the coin name around the English-speaking world, so each country kept a dollar of its own.
senses.whyCN: 贸易与殖民把这种钱币的名字带到整个英语世界，各国于是各自保留了自己的元。

intro.en: Dollar traces to a silver coin minted in a Bohemian valley, whose German name passed through Dutch into English.
intro.cn: dollar 可追溯到波希米亚一处山谷铸造的银币，其德语名称经荷兰语进入英语。

items.en: Joachimstaler named a silver coin from Joachimstal, the valley of Saint Joachim.
items.cn: Joachimstaler 指来自圣约阿希姆山谷的银币。

items.en: The long name was shortened to Taler, a large silver coin used across central Europe.
items.cn: 这个长名被缩短为 Taler，指中欧流通的大银元。

items.en: Dutch daler carried the coin name into sea trade and English ports.
items.cn: 荷兰语 daler 把这个钱币名带进海上贸易与英国港口。

items.en: English dollar first named various large silver coins, including the Spanish piece of eight.
items.cn: 英语 dollar 最初指多种大银币，包括西班牙的八里亚尔银币。

items.en: After independence the United States chose dollar as the name of its national currency.
items.cn: 独立后，美国选用 dollar 作为本国货币的名称。

items.en: Canada, Australia and New Zealand likewise named their currencies dollars.
items.cn: 加拿大、澳大利亚与新西兰也把各自的货币称作 dollar。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the coin name and its compounds; the near-meaning group names other money words.
note.cn: 形近组共享这枚钱币的名称及其复合词；近义组收的是其他表示钱的词。

entries.definition: The process of a country adopting the US dollar as its currency.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「美元化」，指一国改用美元作货币的过程。

entries.definition: US dollars earned from selling oil.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「石油美元」，指卖石油所得的美元收入。

entries.definition: The German silver coin whose name became dollar.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指德国的塔勒银币，dollar 的名称正由它而来。

entries.definition: An informal American word for one dollar.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，美式口语，义为「一美元」。

entries.definition: The general word for a country's system of money.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「货币、通货」，指一国货币体系的通称。

entries.definition: A piece of metal money, smaller in scope than dollar.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「硬币」，范围比 dollar 窄。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the coin's real journey from a German valley to American pockets.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着这枚钱币的真实旅程，从德国山谷走到美国人的口袋。

normal.en: Joachimstal was a silver valley; Joachimstaler was the coin it produced.
normal.cn: 约阿希姆谷出产白银，那里铸出的银币就叫 Joachimstaler。

normal.en: Taler shortened the name, and Dutch daler shortened it further.
normal.cn: Taler 缩短了这个名字，荷兰语 daler 又把它缩短了一次。

normal.en: A dollar bill is paper; a dollar coin is metal; both are one unit.
normal.cn: 纸币与硬币都可能是 dollar，两者都代表一个单位。

normal.en: The dollar sign is a written shorthand for the same unit.
normal.cn: 美元符号就是同一个单位的书写简写。

normal.en: Canadian and Australian dollars show how far the name travelled.
normal.cn: 加拿大元与澳元说明这个名字走得多远。

abstract.en: Picture a silver coin stamped with a valley's name, worn smooth by many hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚刻着山谷名字的银币，被许多只手磨得发亮。

abstract.en: Picture a folded note straightened on a shop counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一张折过的纸币在柜台上被摊平。

abstract.en: Picture one coin passing from a harbour in Europe to a till in America.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币从欧洲的港口一路走到美洲的收银机。

examples.en: The book costs ten dollars in the campus shop.
examples.cn: 这本书在校园商店卖十美元。

examples.en: Every dollar raised will go to the clinic.
examples.cn: 筹到的每一美元都会用于这家诊所。

examples.en: He slipped a dollar into the busker's hat.
examples.cn: 他把一美元塞进街头艺人的帽子里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「多乐」——口袋里多几枚硬币就多几分乐，dollar 就是钱。

root: dollar 源自德语 Joachimstaler，指波希米亚圣约阿希姆谷铸造的大银币，后缩短为 Taler，经荷兰语 daler 进入英语。它与拉丁语没有同族关系，词根不可拆作拉丁成分。

sensesIntro.en: One coin name covers the American unit, a single note or coin, and the units of several other countries.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个钱币名称，覆盖美国的货币单位、一张纸币或一枚硬币，以及若干其他国家的货币单位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worn silver coin and a straightened paper note, both worth one unit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚磨旧的银币与一张摊平的纸币，都值一个单位。

branches.en: THE UNIT: the dollar as the standard measure of American money.
branches.cn: 单位线：dollar 作为美国货币的标准计量单位。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: one unit held as a coin or a folded note.
branches.cn: 实物线：以硬币或折叠纸币形式拿在手里的一元。

branches.en: THE COPY: other countries keep their own dollars on the same pattern.
branches.cn: 各国线：别的国家照着同一模式保留自己的元。

branches.en: The abstract unit and the physical note share one name because the note carries the unit.
branches.cn: 抽象单位与实体纸币共用一个名称，因为纸币承载着这个单位。

branches.en: The American unit and the foreign units are siblings of one old coin name.
branches.cn: 美国的单位与别国的单位是同一个古老钱币名的兄弟。

intro.en: Dollar is a borrowed coin name; English expands it with suffixes and combining forms rather than a Latin root.
intro.cn: dollar 是借来的钱币名，英语靠后缀与组合形式扩展它，而不是靠拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognate exists for this German coin name, so the Latin entry list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个德语钱币名没有拉丁同族词，所以拉丁条目留空。

items.meaningCN: 来自约阿希姆谷的银币
items.example: The long name was later shortened.
The thaler circulated across central Europe.
The dollar is strong this year.
She saved fifty dollars.
The small economy dollarized its savings.
items.exampleCN: 这个小经济体把储蓄美元化了。

items.meaning: the process of adopting the dollar
items.example: Dollarization followed the currency crisis.
items.exampleCN: 货币危机之后出现了美元化。

items.example: It forms petrodollar.
It forms eurodollar.

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ization 构成，义为「美元化」，指一国改用美元作流通货币
由 petro-「石油」加本词构成，义为「石油美元」
由本词加 -ize 构成，义为「使美元化」

definition_zh: 家庭的；家务的；国内的；驯养的
definition_en: relating to the home or family, to one's own country, or to animals kept by people
core_image: 厨房窗台上晾着洗好的碗，楼下传来自家孩子的脚步声
scene: 周末早晨厨房里飘着面包香，孩子还在客厅搭积木。Domestic chores fall to her on Sundays.
sceneCN: 这里 domestic 是「家庭的、家务的」（第 1 个义项：与家庭和家务有关）；句意是星期天大部分家务都落在她身上。

pos.zh: 形容词：家庭的；家务的；国内的；驯养的
名词：家仆（旧用法，多用于英式英语）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加动词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「驯化；使适应家庭生活」
由 domesticate 加 -ion 构成，义为「驯化；归化」
由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「家庭生活；恋家」
由 domesticate 加 -ed 构成，义为「已驯化的；习惯家庭生活的」

senses.title: Of the home and household
senses.definition: relating to the home, the household or family life
senses.definitionCN: 与家、家庭生活或家务有关的
senses.example: They argued about how to share domestic work.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为如何分担家务争吵过。
senses.why: Latin domus meant house, so the adjective begins as a word about everything inside the walls of a home.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 domus 是「房子」，所以这个形容词一开始就指家门以内的一切。

senses.title: Within one country
senses.definition: relating to one's own country rather than to foreign countries
senses.definitionCN: 与本国内部有关，而非与外国有关的
senses.example: Domestic flights leave from the older terminal.
senses.exampleCN: 国内航班从较旧的航站楼出发。
senses.why: A country is imagined as a large household, so affairs inside its borders are domestic affairs.
senses.whyCN: 一个国家被想象成一个大家庭，因此国境之内的事务就是「家里的」事务。

senses.title: Tamed, not wild
senses.definition: kept by people as a pet or farm animal rather than living in the wild
senses.definitionCN: 由人饲养作宠物或农用，而非野生生活的
senses.example: The farm keeps both domestic and wild species.
senses.exampleCN: 这个农场既养家养品种，也养野生物种。
senses.why: An animal brought into the house or the yard has crossed the same boundary as a household matter.
senses.whyCN: 被带进屋里或院里的动物，和家务事一样跨过了「家门」这条界线。

intro.en: Domestic comes from Latin domesticus, belonging to the house, and the root domus, house.
intro.cn: domestic 来自拉丁语 domesticus（属于家的），其根是 domus（房子）。

items.en: The root behind domus is generally reconstructed as a word for house or household; the exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: domus 背后的词根一般重构为表示「房子、家户」的形式，具体形态不确定。

items.en: Domus meant a house or a household, and it produced dominus, the master of the house.
items.cn: domus 指房子或家户，它还生出 dominus（一家之主）。

items.en: Domesticus meant belonging to the household, and it was also used for household servants.
items.cn: domesticus 表示「属于家户的」，也用来指家仆。

items.en: Old French domestique passed the adjective into English with both the home and the servant senses.
items.cn: 古法语 domestique 把这个形容词带入英语，家庭义与家仆义一并传入。

items.en: English extended the word from the household to the nation, speaking of domestic affairs.
items.cn: 英语把它从家户扩展到国家，开始说 domestic affairs（国内事务）。

items.en: The adjective now covers chores, flights, animals and products of a whole country.
items.cn: 今天这个形容词覆盖家务、航班、动物，以及一国的产品。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin domus root; the near-meaning group gathers household and internal words.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语 domus 词根；近义组收的是家庭与「内部」类的词。

entries.definition: To tame an animal or bring it into human use.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「驯化、使家养」，由本词加 -ate 构成。

entries.definition: The quality or state of home life.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「家庭生活、恋家」，同出 domus。

entries.definition: A person's permanent home, from Latin domicilium; it shares domus but has a different spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「住所」，来自拉丁语 domicilium；与 domestic 同出 domus，但拼写路径不同。

entries.definition: All the people living together in one home; often used before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「家户、家庭的」，指同住一屋的人。

entries.definition: Inside a country or organisation; the usual word in political contexts for domestic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「内部的」，在政治语境中常与 domestic 对应。

entries.definition: An animal that is no longer wild; narrower than domestic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「驯服的」，范围比 domestic 的驯养义更窄。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real domus family from the house to the nation.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的 domus 词族，从房子一直走到国家。

normal.en: Domus is house; domesticus is what belongs to the house.
normal.cn: domus 是房子，domesticus 就是属于这座房子的。

normal.en: Dominus, master of the house, comes from the same domus.
normal.cn: dominus 意为一家之主，也出自同一个 domus。

normal.en: A domestic flight stays inside the country, as if the nation were one house.
normal.cn: 国内航班留在国境之内，仿佛整个国家是一间大房子。

normal.en: Domestic animals have been brought into the human household.
normal.cn: 家养动物已经被带进了人类的家庭。

normal.en: Gross domestic product counts what is produced inside those borders.
normal.cn: 国内生产总值算的是这些边界之内生产的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a warm kitchen seen from the street, with one lamp still on.
abstract.cn: 想象从街上望见一间温暖的厨房，还亮着一盏灯。

abstract.en: Picture a map of one country drawn as a single house.
abstract.cn: 想象把一国的地图画成一间房子。

abstract.en: Picture a fence where wild grass stops and a swept yard begins.
abstract.cn: 想象一道篱笆，外面是野草，里面是扫干净的院子。

examples.en: Domestic work should not fall on one person alone.
examples.cn: 家务不应只落在一个人身上。

examples.en: The airline added two new domestic routes.
examples.cn: 这家航空公司新增了两条国内航线。

examples.en: Domestic cats sleep far more than their wild cousins.
examples.cn: 家猫比野外的同类睡得多得多。

dict_mnemonic.text: dom 有「家、屋」的意思，-estic 是形容词后缀：属于这间屋子的，就是家庭的、国内的。

root: 源自拉丁语 domesticus（属于家的），由 domus（房子、家户）加形容词后缀 -icus 构成；domus 同时生出 dominus（一家之主）。古法语 domestique 把家庭义与家仆义传入英语，十六世纪起从家户扩展指国家内部。

sensesIntro.en: One root imagines a house, then stretches it to a nation and to animals brought indoors.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词根先想象一间房子，再把它拉到整个国家，以及被带进屋里的动物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a kitchen seen from the street, warm inside and swept clean.
core.cn: 核心意象：从街上望见的一间厨房，里面温暖，地面扫得干净。

branches.en: THE HOME: the first sense covers everything inside the walls of a house.
branches.cn: 家庭线：第一个义项覆盖家门以内的一切。

branches.en: THE NATION: a country is treated as a large household, so inside affairs are domestic.
branches.cn: 国家线：国家被当作大家庭，因此境内事务称作 domestic。

branches.en: THE YARD: tame animals have crossed the same boundary into human keeping.
branches.cn: 院子线：驯养动物跨过同一条界线，进入人的照料范围。

branches.en: House and country share the word because both are spaces one belongs to.
branches.cn: 家庭与国家共用一个词，因为两者都是人所属的空间。

branches.en: A domestic animal is simply a creature moved into the household.
branches.cn: 家养动物不过是被移进家户的一种生物。

intro.en: Domestic joins the Latin house root domus to the adjective suffix -icus, which English keeps as -ic.
intro.cn: domestic 把拉丁语「房子」词根 domus 接到形容词后缀 -icus 上，英语保留为 -ic。

latinIntro.en: Latin domus, domesticus and dominus are recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European form is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 domus、domesticus 与 dominus 均有记录，只有更早的印欧形式属于重构。

items.example: The noun is the house at the centre of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是这一族词的中心「房子」。

items.example: The adjective already carried the home sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词已带有家庭义。

items.example: It forms domestic.
People domesticated wheat long ago.
items.exampleCN: 人类很久以前就驯化了小麦。

items.example: Domestication changed the dog's body.
He missed the domesticity of his parents' house.
items.exampleCN: 他想念父母家中的家庭生活。

items.example: Her domicile is listed on the form.
It forms domesticity.

derivatives.zh: 由本词加动词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「驯化；使适应家庭生活」
由 domesticate 加 -ion 构成，义为「驯化；归化」
由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「家庭生活；恋家」

definition_zh: 占主导地位的；显性的；最突出的
definition_en: having the greatest power or influence, describing a gene that shows its effect, or standing out most clearly
core_image: 长桌尽头那把椅子，所有人都顺着它的方向说话
scene: 会议室里所有人都看向长桌顶端那个人。One company has become dominant in the local taxi market.
sceneCN: 这里 dominant 是「占主导地位的」（第 1 个义项：在某个范围内拥有最大的权力或影响）；句意是有一家公司在本地出租车市场占了主导地位。

pos.zh: 形容词：占主导地位的；显性的；最突出的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「优势；支配地位」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「占主导地；显性地」
由前缀 pre-「在前」加本词构成，义为「占优势的；主要的」
由前缀 pre- 加同一词根构成，义为「占优势；占多数」

senses.title: Holding the most power
senses.definition: having the greatest power, influence or share within a group, market or place
senses.definitionCN: 在某个群体、市场或地方拥有最大的权力、影响或份额
senses.example: Two firms dominate the market, and both are dominant in pricing.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司主导着市场，二者在定价上都占主导地位。
senses.why: Latin dominus was the master of a household, and dominans described the one who masters; dominant is the state of being that master in a group.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dominus 是一家之主，dominans 描述「正在当家」的人；dominant 就是一个群体里处于这种「主人」状态。

senses.title: Expressed in genetics
senses.definition: describes a gene or trait that appears in the offspring even when only one copy is inherited
senses.definitionCN: 描述只需继承一份就能在后代身上表现出来的基因或性状
senses.example: Brown eyes are dominant over blue eyes in this family.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个家族里，棕眼对蓝眼是显性的。
senses.why: The stronger gene behaves like the master of the household: as long as it is present, its effect is what the body shows.
senses.whyCN: 较强的基因像一家之主：只要它在场，身体表现出来的就是它的效果。

senses.title: Most noticeable
senses.definition: standing out most clearly in a view, a design or a piece of music
senses.definitionCN: 在景色、设计或音乐中最清晰地显露出来的
senses.example: The dominant colour of the room is a deep green.
senses.exampleCN: 这间屋子的主色调是深绿色。
senses.why: What stands highest or appears most often catches the eye first, so it takes over the scene as a master takes over a room.
senses.whyCN: 最高的东西或出现最多的东西最先抓住目光，于是它像主人占据屋子一样占据了整个画面。

intro.en: Dominant is the present participle of Latin dominari, to rule, from dominus, master of a household.
intro.cn: dominant 是拉丁语 dominari（统治）的现在分词，其根是 dominus（一家之主）。

items.en: Domus meant house or household, and it also gave dominus, the master of the house.
items.cn: domus 指房子或家户，并生出 dominus（一家之主）。

items.en: Dominari meant to rule or to have mastery over others.
items.cn: dominari 意为「统治、支配他人」。

items.en: The present participle dominans described someone or something that is ruling at that moment.
items.cn: 现在分词 dominans 描述此刻正在起支配作用的人或物。

items.en: Old French dominant carried the adjective into English usage.
items.cn: 古法语 dominant 把这个形容词带入英语用法。

items.en: English used it for political and social power before science borrowed it for genes.
items.cn: 英语先把它用于政治与社会权力，后来科学才借去指基因。

items.en: The word now also names the most visible colour, note or feature.
items.cn: 今天这个词也用来指最显眼的颜色、音符或特征。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the Latin dominus root; the near-meaning group gathers words for power and prominence.
note.cn: 形近组守着拉丁语 dominus 词根；近义组收的是表示权力与突出地位的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to rule, control or be the most important part.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「支配、控制、占首要地位」，与 dominant 同根。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of being dominant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「优势、支配地位」，指处于 dominant 的状态。

entries.definition: Most common or most noticeable; formed with the prefix pre-.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「占优势的、主要的」，由前缀 pre- 加本词构成。

entries.definition: Most important or most successful at a particular time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「领先的、最重要的」，强调位置靠前。

entries.definition: Having the power to direct or restrain others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「控制性的、起支配作用的」，强调施加约束。

entries.definition: The largest or most important of several things; plainer and less formal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「主要的」，在若干事物中最大或最重要，语气更平实。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real dominus family and the places dominance actually shows.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的 dominus 词族，以及支配地位真正显现的场合。

normal.en: Dominus is the master of a house; dominant is the one acting as master.
normal.cn: dominus 是一家之主，dominant 就是正在当家的那一个。

normal.en: Dominari means to rule, so dominant describes whoever rules the group.
normal.cn: dominari 意为统治，dominant 描述统治这个群体的那一方。

normal.en: A dominant gene speaks loudest even when it is alone.
normal.cn: 显性基因即使只有一份，声音也最响。

normal.en: A dominant colour is the one the eye notices before all others.
normal.cn: 主色调就是眼睛先于其他颜色注意到的那个颜色。

normal.en: Pre- plus dominant gives predominant, a near twin meaning most common.
normal.cn: pre- 加 dominant 得到 predominant，意思接近「最常见、最占优势」。

abstract.en: Picture one chair at the end of a long table, slightly taller than the rest.
abstract.cn: 想象长桌尽头有一把椅子，比其余的都略高一点。

abstract.en: Picture one green wall making every other colour in the room look pale.
abstract.cn: 想象一面绿墙让屋里其他颜色都显得淡了。

abstract.en: Picture a single voice that everyone else unconsciously follows.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音，其他所有人都不自觉地跟着它走。

examples.en: English is the dominant language in international business.
examples.cn: 英语是国际商务中的主导语言。

examples.en: The dominant feature of the valley is a long ridge.
examples.cn: 这个山谷最突出的特征是那道长长的山脊。

examples.en: In this species, dark feathers are dominant over pale ones.
examples.cn: 在这个物种里，深色羽毛对浅色羽毛是显性的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「多密难」——人一多、关系一密，就难分高下；最后站上风的那个就是 dominant。

root: 源自拉丁语 dominans，是 dominari（统治）的现在分词，其根为 dominus（一家之主），再往前是 domus（房子、家户）。因此 dominant 本义是「像主人一样当家、压过别人」，后扩展指显性基因与最突出的特征。

sensesIntro.en: From a master of a household to a ruling firm, a loud gene and the colour that takes over a room.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一家之主，到主导市场的公司，再到声音最响的基因和占满屋子的颜色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one chair at the head of the table that everyone turns toward.
core.cn: 核心意象：长桌尽头那把椅子，所有人都朝向它。

branches.en: POWER: the first sense is the social and economic mastery of a group or market.
branches.cn: 权力线：第一个义项是群体或市场中的社会与经济支配力。

branches.en: HEREDITY: the same mastery appears in a gene that overrides its partner.
branches.cn: 遗传线：同样的支配力出现在压过配对基因的显性基因上。

branches.en: ATTENTION: whatever stands out most takes over the eye's field.
branches.cn: 注意线：最突出的东西占据视野。

branches.en: Power and visibility overlap: the strongest feature is usually the one seen first.
branches.cn: 权力与可见度重叠：最强的特征通常也是最先被看见的。

branches.en: Social dominance and genetic dominance share the image of a master that cannot be ignored.
branches.cn: 社会支配与基因显性共享同一幅画面：一个无法被忽视的主人。

intro.en: Dominant is a Latin present participle in -ans, built on dominus, master of a house.
intro.cn: dominant 是拉丁语以 -ans 结尾的现在分词，其根为 dominus（一家之主）。

latinIntro.en: Latin domus, dominus and dominari are recorded; the title dominus also survives in church language.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 domus、dominus 与 dominari 均有记录；dominus 这一称呼也保留在教会用语中。

items.example: The household is the base of the image.
items.exampleCN: 家户是这幅画面的基底。

items.example: The master sits at the head of the table.
items.exampleCN: 一家之主坐在长桌尽头。

items.example: The verb names the act of ruling.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指统治的动作。

items.example: It became the English adjective dominant.
items.exampleCN: 它变成了英语形容词 dominant。

items.example: It forms dominant from the participle.
items.exampleCN: 它把分词变成 dominant 这一形容词。

items.example: The firm holds dominance in the region.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司在该地区占支配地位。

items.example: One team dominated the match.
items.exampleCN: 一支队伍控制了整场比赛。

items.example: It forms predominant.

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「优势；支配地位」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「占主导地；显性地」
由前缀 pre-「在前」加本词构成，义为「占优势的；主要的」

definition_zh: 支配；控制；占首要地位；高耸于
definition_en: to have power over someone or something, to be the most important feature, or to stand above a place
core_image: 一座塔的影子慢慢铺满整条街道
scene: 半山腰那座塔的影子每天准时铺满整个村子。A single tower dominates the skyline of the old town.
sceneCN: 这里 dominate 是「高耸于、俯瞰」（第 3 个义项：在某处上方高高立起并成为最显眼的景象）；句意是一座孤塔高耸于老城的天际线。

pos.zh: 动词：支配；控制；占首要地位；高耸于

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「支配；统治」
由同一词根构成，义为「占主导地位的；显性的」
由 dominant 加 -ance 构成，义为「优势；支配地位」
由本词加施事后缀 -or 构成，义为「支配者」

senses.title: To control people or places
senses.definition: to have power and influence over a person, group, market or place
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、某群体、市场或地方拥有权力与影响
senses.example: A few large firms dominate the shipping industry.
senses.exampleCN: 几家大公司支配着航运业。
senses.why: The verb comes from dominari, to rule as a master of the house, so dominating is making others live under your direction.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词来自 dominari，即以一家之主的身份统治；所以 dominate 就是让别人在你的指挥下行事。

senses.title: To be the main feature
senses.definition: to be the most important, noticeable or frequent part of something
senses.definitionCN: 成为某事物中最重要、最显眼或出现最多的部分
senses.example: Talk of the storm dominated the evening news.
senses.exampleCN: 有关风暴的消息占据了当晚新闻的主要部分。
senses.why: Whatever occupies the largest share behaves like the master of a room: it sets the tone for everything else.
senses.whyCN: 占据最大份额的东西就像屋子的主人，别的都要跟着它定调。

senses.title: To tower above a place
senses.definition: to stand high above a place and be seen from all around it
senses.definitionCN: 在某处高高立起，从四周都能看见
senses.example: The cathedral dominates the square below it.
senses.exampleCN: 大教堂高耸于它下方的广场之上。
senses.why: A tower that fills the view from every street acts like a master overlooking a household, so the verb extends to height.
senses.whyCN: 从每条街望过去都占满视野的塔，就像俯视家户的主人，于是这个动词又扩展到高度。

intro.en: Dominate is the English verb built on Latin dominari, to rule, and on dominus, master of a household.
intro.cn: dominate 是英语动词，建立在拉丁语 dominari（统治）与 dominus（一家之主）之上。

items.en: Domus, house or household, is the oldest word in the family.
items.cn: domus（房子、家户）是这一族里最古老的词。

items.en: Dominus named the master of the household and later any lord or owner.
items.cn: dominus 指一家之主，后来泛指主人或所有者。

items.en: Dominari meant to rule, to exercise mastery over people or things.
items.cn: dominari 意为统治，对人施加支配。

items.en: The participle dominatus described something ruled or controlled.
items.cn: 分词 dominatus 描述被统治、被控制的状态。

items.en: English formed the verb dominate from the Latin stem; exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁词干造出动词 dominate，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The sense widened from people to markets, conversations and towers on a skyline.
items.cn: 词义从人扩展到市场、谈话，以及天际线上的塔。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the domin stem; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of control and prominence.
note.cn: 形近组守着 domin 词干；近义组收的是表示控制与突出地位的动词。

entries.definition: The adjective describing whoever or whatever dominates.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「占主导地位的」，描述正在支配的那一方。

entries.definition: The noun for the act or state of dominating.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「支配、统治」，指支配的行为或状态。

entries.definition: A person or thing that dominates.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「支配者」，指施行支配的人或物。

entries.definition: To direct or restrain something; it stresses management rather than superiority.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「控制、管理」，强调管理而非地位高低。

entries.definition: To prove stronger in the end, often after a struggle.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「占上风、最终取胜」，常含经过较量之意。

entries.definition: To be more important or noticeable than something else, or to cast shade over it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使相形见绌、遮蔽」，兼有更重要与投下阴影两义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real dominus family and the three arenas where dominating happens.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的 dominus 词族，以及支配发生的三种场合。

normal.en: Dominus is the master, so dominate is to act as that master.
normal.cn: dominus 是主人，dominate 就是扮演这个主人。

normal.en: Domination and dominator come straight from the same stem.
normal.cn: domination 与 dominator 直接从同一词干变来。

normal.en: Markets, talks and games can all be dominated by one side.
normal.cn: 市场、谈话与比赛都可能被一方主导。

normal.en: A tower dominates a skyline by filling the view from every street.
normal.cn: 塔高耸于天际线，是因为从每条街望过去都占满视野。

normal.en: The passive form be dominated by means the power lies with someone else.
normal.cn: 被动形式 be dominated by 表示权力在别人手里。

abstract.en: Picture a long shadow from one tower reaching every roof in the town.
abstract.cn: 想象一座塔投下长长的影子，伸到镇上的每一片屋顶。

abstract.en: Picture one voice speaking while the others only nod.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音在说话，其他人只是点头。

abstract.en: Picture a single name on a scoreboard far ahead of the rest.
abstract.cn: 想象计分板上只有一个名字远远领先。

examples.en: One chain dominates the coffee market in this city.
examples.cn: 一家连锁店主导着这座城市的咖啡市场。

examples.en: The argument dominated dinner conversation for an hour.
examples.cn: 这场争论占据晚餐谈话长达一小时。

examples.en: A tall clock tower dominates the harbour.
examples.cn: 一座高高的钟楼高耸于港口之上。

dict_mnemonic.text: domin 有「主人、当家」的意思，-ate 是动词后缀：像主人一样当家，就是支配、控制。

root: 源自拉丁语 dominari（统治），由 dominus（一家之主）派生，再往前是 domus（房子、家户）。本义是像主人一样对人和物行使支配，后来引申为在某事物中占最大份额，以及在高处俯瞰一片地方。

sensesIntro.en: One verb covers ruling people, filling a conversation or market, and rising above a whole town.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个动词覆盖了统治他人、占满谈话或市场，以及高高矗立在一座城镇之上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tower whose shadow reaches every street in the town.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座塔，影子伸到镇上的每一条街。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND MARKETS: the first sense is direct power over others.
branches.cn: 人物与市场线：第一个义项是对他人的直接支配。

branches.en: THE SHARE: the second sense is dominance measured in attention or quantity.
branches.cn: 份额线：第二个义项是以注意力或数量衡量的主导。

branches.en: HEIGHT: the third sense is physical dominance over a view.
branches.cn: 高度线：第三个义项是在视野中的物理性高踞。

branches.en: Power over people and power over a conversation are two scales of the same mastery.
branches.cn: 对人的支配与对谈话的支配，是同一股当家之势的两种尺度。

branches.en: Whatever fills the view or the talk is simply the most dominant thing present.
branches.cn: 占满视野或占满谈话的东西，都只是当下最占主导的那一个。

intro.en: Dominate takes the Latin verb suffix -ate onto the same dominus stem.
intro.cn: dominate 把拉丁语动词后缀 -ate 接到同一个 dominus 词干上。

latinIntro.en: Latin dominus and dominari are recorded; the noun dominatio also existed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dominus 与 dominari 均有记录，名词 dominatio 也存在。

items.example: The master is the source of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 主人是这一动词的来源。

items.example: The verb already meant to rule.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词本义就是统治。

items.example: It forms dominate.
The domination lasted for years.
He acted as the dominator of the group.
items.exampleCN: 他充当这个群体的支配者。

items.example: The dominant team scored first.
They lost dominance in the market.
items.exampleCN: 他们失去了市场支配地位。

items.example: Pine trees predominate on the ridge.

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「支配；统治」
由同一词根构成，义为「占主导地位的；显性的」
由本词加施事后缀 -or 构成，义为「支配者」

definition_zh: 捐赠；捐款；捐赠物；血液或器官捐献
definition_en: the act of giving money, goods, blood or an organ to help others, or the thing given
core_image: 一只透明的募捐箱，箱底铺满硬币
scene: 医院大厅摆着一只透明的募捐箱，箱底已经铺了一层硬币。The charity received a large donation from a local factory.
sceneCN: 这里 donation 是「捐款、捐赠物」（第 2 个义项：捐出的钱或物）；句意是这家慈善机构收到了本地一家工厂的一大笔捐款。

pos.zh: 名词：捐赠；捐款；捐赠物；血液或器官捐献

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干加动词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「捐赠；捐献」
由拉丁词干加施事后缀 -or 构成，义为「捐赠者；捐献者」
由拉丁词干加后缀构成，义为「捐赠的；捐赠物」（较少用）

senses.title: The act of giving
senses.definition: the act of giving money or goods to a charity, a cause or a person in need
senses.definitionCN: 把钱或物捐给慈善机构、某项事业或需要帮助的人的行为
senses.example: The donation of the old library building saved it from demolition.
senses.exampleCN: 旧图书馆建筑的捐赠使它免于被拆除。
senses.why: Latin donare meant to give, and donatio named the giving itself before it named the object given.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 donare 意为「给」，donatio 先指给予这一行为，后来才指所给之物。

senses.title: Something given
senses.definition: money or goods that are given in this way
senses.definitionCN: 以这种方式捐出的钱或物品
senses.example: A pile of donations filled the back of the truck.
senses.exampleCN: 一车捐赠物堆满了卡车后厢。
senses.why: The act leaves a result behind, and that result becomes the countable thing we call a donation.
senses.whyCN: 行为会留下结果，这个结果就成了可以数的「一笔捐赠、一件捐赠物」。

senses.title: Blood or organ donation
senses.definition: the giving of blood, tissue or an organ for medical treatment
senses.definitionCN: 为医疗用途捐出血液、组织或器官
senses.example: Regular blood donation helps hospitals keep enough supply.
senses.exampleCN: 定期献血帮助医院维持足够的库存。
senses.why: The same generous giving now applies to the body itself, where the gift can save a life directly.
senses.whyCN: 同样慷慨的给予如今落到身体本身，这份礼物能直接救一条命。

intro.en: Donation comes from Latin donatio, a giving, built on donum, gift, and donare, to give.
intro.cn: donation 来自拉丁语 donatio（给予），其根为 donum（礼物）与 donare（给）。

items.en: The root behind donum is generally reconstructed as a word for giving; its exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: donum 背后的词根一般重构为表示「给」的形式，具体形态不确定。

items.en: Donum meant a gift, something handed over without payment.
items.cn: donum 指礼物，即无偿交出的东西。

items.en: Donare meant to give, present or grant.
items.cn: donare 意为「给、赠予、授予」。

items.en: Donatio named the act of giving and also the gift itself in legal language.
items.cn: donatio 既指给予的行为，在法律用语里也指赠与之物。

items.en: Old French donation carried the word into English with its charitable tone.
items.cn: 古法语 donation 把这个词带入英语，同时带来慈善色彩。

items.en: Modern medicine added blood and organ donation to the older sense of giving money.
items.cn: 现代医学在「捐钱」这一旧义之外，又加上献血与器官捐献。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin giving root; the near-meaning group gathers other forms of contribution.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「给」的词根；近义组收的是其他形式的贡献。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to give money, goods or blood to a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「捐赠、捐献」，与 donation 同根。

entries.definition: A person or organisation that gives, especially blood or an organ.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「捐赠者、捐献者」，尤指献血或捐器官的人。

entries.definition: A rare adjective or noun for something given as a gift.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「捐赠的；捐赠物」，较少使用。

entries.definition: Money or help given toward a shared purpose; broader and less emotional.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「贡献、捐款」，指为共同目标给出的钱或帮助，范围更广。

entries.definition: Something given to a person, often for pleasure rather than charity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「礼物」，常出于心意而非慈善。

entries.definition: Money given by an institution for a specific purpose, usually after an application.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「拨款、补助金」，通常由机构在申请后给出。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real donum family and the three kinds of giving it now covers.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的 donum 词族，以及它今天覆盖的三种给予。

normal.en: Donum is a gift; donare is to give; donatio is the giving.
normal.cn: donum 是礼物，donare 是给，donatio 是给予这件事。

normal.en: Donate, donor and donation all keep the same giving stem.
normal.cn: donate、donor 与 donation 都保留同一个「给」的词干。

normal.en: A donation can be a sum of money or the act of writing the cheque.
normal.cn: donation 既可以是那笔钱，也可以是写支票这个行为。

normal.en: Blood donation is the same gift applied to the body.
normal.cn: 献血是把同一份礼物用在身体上。

normal.en: A donor is the person on the giving side of the noun.
normal.cn: donor 就是这件事里站在给予一方的人。

abstract.en: Picture a clear box slowly filling with coins at a hospital door.
abstract.cn: 想象医院门口一只透明箱子，硬币一点点堆起来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand passing a folded note across a counter and letting go.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把折好的纸币递过柜台，然后松开。

abstract.en: Picture one arm offered while another person waits for help.
abstract.cn: 想象一条手臂伸出来，另一个人在等着这份帮助。

examples.en: The school received a donation of thirty new desks.
examples.cn: 学校收到捐赠的三十张新课桌。

examples.en: She made a small monthly donation to the animal shelter.
examples.cn: 她每月向动物收容所捐一小笔钱。

examples.en: The clinic urgently needs blood donations of the rarest type.
examples.cn: 这家诊所急需最稀有血型的献血。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「兜内」——把兜里的钱拿出来放进募捐箱，就是一份 donation。

root: 源自拉丁语 donatio（给予），由 donare（给）加名词后缀 -tio 构成，其根为 donum（礼物）。本义是「无偿给予」这一行为，后来既指捐出的钱物，也扩展到献血与器官捐献。

sensesIntro.en: One giving root covers the act, the thing given, and the gift of blood or an organ.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「给」的词根，覆盖给予的行为、所给之物，以及血液或器官这份礼物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear collection box with coins settled at the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只透明募捐箱，硬币沉在箱底。

branches.en: THE ACT: the first sense is the giving itself, before any object is counted.
branches.cn: 行为线：第一个义项是给予本身，尚未去数具体东西。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the second sense is what the act leaves behind in the box.
branches.cn: 实物线：第二个义项是行为留在箱子里的东西。

branches.en: THE BODY: the third sense gives blood or an organ instead of money.
branches.cn: 身体线：第三个义项给的不是钱，而是血或器官。

branches.en: The act and the object share one noun because a gift exists only through being given.
branches.cn: 行为与实物共用一个名词，因为礼物正是通过被给出才存在。

branches.en: Money and blood are both things handed over so that someone else can live better.
branches.cn: 钱与血都是交出去、好让别人的日子好过一些的东西。

intro.en: Donation is a Latin action noun in -tio built on donare, to give, and donum, gift.
intro.cn: donation 是拉丁语以 -tio 结尾的动作名词，建立在 donare（给）与 donum（礼物）之上。

latinIntro.en: Latin donum, donare and donatio are recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 donum、donare 与 donatio 均有记录，只有更早的印欧词根属于重构。

items.example: The noun is the gift itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词就是礼物本身。

items.example: The verb names the act of giving.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指给予的动作。

items.example: The Latin noun became English donation.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词变成了英语 donation。

items.example: It forms donation.
They donated warm coats.
The donor wished to remain unnamed.
items.exampleCN: 这位捐赠者希望不留名。

items.example: It forms donor.
It forms donate.

由拉丁词干加施事后缀 -or 构成，义为「捐赠者；捐献者」
由拉丁词干加后缀构成，义为「捐赠的；捐赠物」（较少用）

definition_en: a small horse-like animal with long ears, a foolish person, or the dull hard work called donkey work
core_image: 山道上一头驮着两袋玉米的小牲口，耳朵又长又直
scene: 山道上，一头灰褐色的小牲口驮着两袋玉米慢慢往前挪。The donkey stopped beside the well and refused to move.
sceneCN: 这里 donkey 是「驴」（第 1 个义项：一种耳朵很长、常用来驮物的家畜）；句意是那头驴在井边停下，怎么也不肯走。

pos.zh: 名词：驴；蠢人；苦差事

collocations.zh: 苦差事；单调繁重的工作

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 work 构成的复合词，义为「单调繁重的苦差事」
由本词加 jacket 构成的复合词，义为「工装夹克」
由本词加 years 构成的习语，义为「很长时间」

senses.title: A load-carrying animal
senses.definition: a small animal like a horse, with long ears, often used for carrying loads
senses.definitionCN: 一种像马的小型动物，耳朵很长，常用来驮东西
senses.example: A donkey carried the sacks up the narrow path.
senses.exampleCN: 一头驴驮着口袋走上狭窄的山道。
senses.why: The word named the familiar working animal of farms and hill paths, the one that carries what people cannot.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先指农庄与山道上最常见的工作牲口，也就是替人驮东西的那一只。

senses.title: A foolish or stubborn person
senses.definition: a foolish or stubborn person, used informally and often as an insult
senses.definitionCN: 愚蠢或固执的人，属非正式用法，常带侮辱意味
senses.example: Don't be a donkey and sign without reading it.
senses.exampleCN: 别犯傻看都不看就签字。
senses.why: The animal's reputation for stubbornness turned its name into a mild insult for a person who will not listen.
senses.whyCN: 这种动物以固执出名，名字便成了对不肯听话之人的轻蔑称呼。

senses.title: Dull hard work
senses.definition: used in the phrase donkey work for tiring, repetitive work that others avoid
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 donkey work，指别人不愿干的累人而重复的工作
senses.example: The interns did the donkey work of sorting old files.
senses.exampleCN: 实习生干了整理旧档案这类苦差事。
senses.why: The animal that carries loads without complaint supplies the image for work that is heavy and repetitive.
senses.whyCN: 那种默默驮重物的牲口，正好为繁重又重复的工作提供了画面。

intro.en: Donkey appeared in English in the eighteenth century and its origin is uncertain, though several explanations exist.
intro.cn: donkey 在十八世纪出现于英语，来源不确定，虽有几种解释但都未定论。

items.en: The older word for the animal was ass, from Latin asinus, and it is unrelated to donkey.
items.cn: 这种动物早先叫 ass，来自拉丁语 asinus，与 donkey 没有词源关系。

items.en: Donkey is first recorded in the eighteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: donkey 最早在十八世纪有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: One common suggestion links it to dun, a dull brown colour, plus a suffix; this remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: 一种常见说法把它与 dun（暗淡的褐色）加后缀联系起来，但这仍只是假说。

items.en: Another suggestion derives it from a proper name such as Duncan, but no explanation is proven.
items.cn: 另一种说法认为它来自 Duncan 之类的人名，但没有任何解释得到证实。

items.en: The informal sense of a foolish person and the phrase donkey work both spread in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 「蠢人」的口语义与 donkey work 这一说法都在十九世纪流行起来。

items.en: The animal name now also supplies compounds such as donkey jacket and donkey's years.
items.cn: 这个动物名今天还提供 donkey jacket 与 donkey's years 等说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds built on the animal name; the near-meaning group names other load-bearing beasts.
note.cn: 形近组收的是围绕这个动物名构成的复合说法；近义组收的是其他驮运牲口。

entries.definition: Tiring, repetitive work that few people want to do.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「苦差事」，指几乎没人愿意干的累人重复工作。

entries.definition: A short heavy work jacket, originally worn by labourers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「工装夹克」，最初是体力劳动者穿的厚短外套。

entries.definition: A very long time, used in informal British speech.
entries.definitionCN: 习语，义为「很久、多年」，属非正式英式说法。

entries.definition: The older English word for a donkey, also used for a foolish person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「驴」，也指蠢人；是这种动物的旧称。

entries.definition: The offspring of a donkey and a horse, also used for a stubborn person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「骡」，也指固执的人；是驴与马的后代。

entries.definition: A small donkey, especially one used in Spanish-speaking regions.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小毛驴」，多用于西班牙语地区。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the animal's real working life and the phrases English built from its name.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用这种动物真实的工作生活，以及英语由它名字造出的说法。

normal.en: The older word was ass, so donkey is a newer name for the same beast.
normal.cn: 旧称是 ass，donkey 只是同一头牲口后来的新名字。

normal.en: Donkey work is the heavy, repetitive part nobody wants.
normal.cn: donkey work 就是没人愿意干的繁重重复部分。

normal.en: A donkey jacket is work clothing, not something worn by an animal.
normal.cn: donkey jacket 是工装，不是驴穿的外套。

normal.en: Donkey's years means a long time, not an animal's age.
normal.cn: donkey's years 指很久，不是动物的岁数。

normal.en: Calling a person a donkey is an informal insult about stubbornness.
normal.cn: 把人叫作 donkey，是关于固执的非正式侮辱。

abstract.en: Picture long ears beside a well, refusing to take one more step.
abstract.cn: 想象井边一双长耳朵，怎么也不肯再走一步。

abstract.en: Picture two sacks of corn strapped to a small back on a steep path.
abstract.cn: 想象陡峭山道上，两袋玉米绑在一副小小的背上。

abstract.en: Picture a worker carrying the dull load while others talk.
abstract.cn: 想象别人在说话，一个工人却扛着那份枯燥的重活。

examples.en: The donkey carried water up the hill every morning.
examples.cn: 那头驴每天早上驮水上山。

examples.en: Someone has to do the donkey work before the event.
examples.cn: 活动之前总得有人干那些苦差事。

examples.en: I have not seen that shop for donkey's years.
examples.cn: 我很久没见那家店了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「当骑」——山路上驮着东西、当坐骑的那头牲口，就是 donkey。

root: donkey 于十八世纪出现于英语，来源不确定；较旧的同类词是 ass（拉丁语 asinus）。常见假说把它与表示暗褐色的 dun 加后缀联系起来，也有来自人名的说法，均未获证实。驴的固执形象又派生出「蠢人」义与 donkey work 等说法。

sensesIntro.en: One animal name gives the load carrier, a stubborn person, and the heavy work nobody wants.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个动物名，既给出驮物的牲口，也给出固执的人，还给出没人愿干的繁重活。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small long-eared animal carrying sacks up a steep path.
core.cn: 核心意象：一头长耳朵的小牲口，驮着口袋走在陡坡上。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL: the first sense is the working donkey on farm and hill paths.
branches.cn: 动物线：第一个义项是农庄与山道上的役用驴。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the second sense transfers the animal's stubborn image to a person.
branches.cn: 人物线：第二个义项把这种动物的固执形象移到人身上。

branches.en: THE WORK: the third sense turns patient load carrying into a phrase for dull labour.
branches.cn: 工作线：第三个义项把默默驮重变成指枯燥劳动的说法。

branches.en: The beast and the burden explain each other: the animal is named for the work it does.
branches.cn: 牲口与重活互相解释：这种动物正是因它所干的活而被使用。

branches.en: A stubborn person and an unpleasant task share the same stubborn animal image.
branches.cn: 固执的人与难缠的活共享同一幅固执动物的画面。

intro.en: Donkey has no Latin root; English builds its phrases and compounds from the animal name itself.
intro.cn: donkey 没有拉丁词根，英语直接用这个动物名搭出短语与复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin word for a donkey was asinus, but it is not a cognate, so no Latin family is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语里驴叫 asinus，但它并非同源词，所以这里不列拉丁词族。

items.example: A donkey stood by the gate.
Dun is one suggested source of the name.
items.exampleCN: dun 是这个名字的一种假想来源。

items.example: The ending has no agreed meaning.

The donkey work took all afternoon.

items.example: He wore a dark donkey jacket.

definition_en: a panel that opens and closes an entrance, the entrance itself, or a way of reaching something
core_image: 走廊尽头一扇半开的木门，门缝里透出一线光
scene: 走廊尽头那扇木门半开着，里头透出一线灯光。He knocked twice before the door opened.
sceneCN: 这里 door 是「门」（第 1 个义项：可开合的门板）；句意是他敲了两下，门才打开。

pos.zh: 名词：门；门口；途径

senses.title: A movable panel
senses.definition: a flat panel, usually of wood or metal, that opens and closes the entrance to a room, building or vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 通常为木或金属的平板，用来开合房间、建筑或车辆的入口
senses.example: The old door creaked whenever someone entered.
senses.exampleCN: 每次有人进门，那扇旧门就吱呀作响。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the thing you push or pull, the panel that physically seals an opening.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是那块你推或拉的东西，那块真正把开口封住的门板。

senses.title: The entrance space
senses.definition: the entrance of a building or room, or the space just inside or outside it
senses.definitionCN: 建筑或房间的入口，也包括紧挨入口的内外空间
senses.example: A stranger was waiting at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 有个陌生人在门口等着。
senses.why: Once the panel is the landmark, the space around it is named after it too, so people stand at the door.
senses.whyCN: 门板一旦成了地标，它周围的空间也跟着以它命名，于是人们会「站在门口」。

senses.title: A way to reach something
senses.definition: a means of gaining access to an opportunity, a place or a group
senses.definitionCN: 获得机会、进入某地或加入某群体的手段
senses.example: A good education opens doors that money cannot.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的教育能打开金钱打不开的门。
senses.why: A real door controls who may pass, so any controlled access to opportunity borrows the same image.
senses.whyCN: 真实的门决定谁能通过，因此任何通往机会的受控入口都借用了这同一幅画面。

intro.en: Door is an Old English word with Germanic and Indo-European relatives, not a Latin borrowing.
intro.cn: door 是古英语词，有日耳曼语与印欧语亲属，并非拉丁语借词。

items.en: The root is generally reconstructed as *dhwer-, a word for a door or gate; the exact form is reconstructed.
items.cn: 这个词根一般重构为 *dhwer-，表示门或大门，具体形态属于重构。

items.en: The Germanic form *dur- appears in words for doors across the northern languages.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式 *dur- 出现在北方各语言表示「门」的词里。

items.en: Old English had duru for a single door and dor for a doorway or gate.
items.cn: 古英语 duru 指单扇门，dor 指门道或大门。

items.en: The two forms merged into the modern word door.
items.cn: 两个形式合并成了现代词 door。

items.en: The figurative sense of a door to opportunity appears in religious and literary writing.
items.cn: 「机会之门」的比喻义在宗教与文学写作中出现。

items.en: Door now supplies a large family of compounds, from doorbell to doorway.
items.cn: 今天 door 提供了一大批复合词，从门铃到门口。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds built on door; the near-meaning group names other openings.
note.cn: 形近组收的是围绕 door 构成的复合词；近义组收的是其他开口。

entries.definition: The opening in a wall where a door is fitted.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「门口、门道」，指墙上装门的开口。

entries.definition: A person employed to guard the entrance of a building.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「门卫、门房」，指受雇看守入口的人。

entries.definition: A bell pushed by visitors to announce their arrival.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「门铃」，访客按响以告知到来的铃。

entries.definition: A barrier in a fence or wall, usually outdoors and larger than a door.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大门、栅门」，通常在户外，比 door 更大。

entries.definition: The point where you enter a place; it may have no door at all.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「入口」，指进入某处的点，未必有门板。

entries.definition: A large or impressive entrance, often used figuratively for a gateway to something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「门户、入口」，常作比喻指通往某物的门户，语气正式。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English word and the compounds English built from it.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用真实的古英语词，以及英语由它构成的复合词。

normal.en: Old English duru and dor merged into door.
normal.cn: 古英语的 duru 与 dor 合并成了 door。

normal.en: The same ancient root appears in the Germanic words for door.
normal.cn: 同一个古老词根出现在日耳曼各语言表示「门」的词里。

normal.en: A doorway is the opening, not the panel that fills it.
normal.cn: doorway 指开口，不是填在开口里的门板。

normal.en: A doorman guards the entrance; the compound adds a person.
normal.cn: doorman 看守入口，复合词加上了一个人。

normal.en: Open doors is a figurative phrase for giving access to opportunity.
normal.cn: open doors 是比喻说法，指打开通往机会的路。

abstract.en: Picture a thin line of light under a closed wooden door.
abstract.cn: 想象紧闭的木门下透出一条细光。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a brass handle, pausing before turning it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手放在铜把手上，转动之前停了一停。

abstract.en: Picture a corridor of identical doors, one of them slightly open.
abstract.cn: 想象一走廊一模一样的门，其中一扇微微开着。

examples.en: Please shut the door when you leave the office.
examples.cn: 离开办公室时请把门关上。

examples.en: Someone is standing at the door and asking for you.
examples.cn: 有人站在门口找你。

examples.en: The scholarship opened a door to a better school.
examples.cn: 这笔奖学金打开了通往更好学校的一扇门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「多」——屋里屋外多一些门，进进出出都要经过它；door 就是门。

root: door 是古英语 duru（单扇门）与 dor（门道）的合并形式，往上可追到日耳曼语 *dur- 与重构的印欧词根 *dhwer-；它不是拉丁语借词。后由实体的门引申出「门口」与「机会之门」的比喻义。

sensesIntro.en: From the wooden panel itself, to the space around it, and finally to any controlled way into opportunity.
sensesIntro.cn: 从木质门板本身，到它周围的空间，最后延伸到任何通往机会的受控入口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a half-open wooden door with a line of light along its edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇半开的木门，边缘透出一线光。

branches.en: THE PANEL: the physical board that seals or opens the entrance.
branches.cn: 门板线：真正封住或打开入口的那块板。

branches.en: THE THRESHOLD: the entrance and the space just inside or outside it.
branches.cn: 门槛线：入口，以及紧挨入口的内外空间。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: control of access becomes an image for opportunity.
branches.cn: 比喻线：对进出的控制变成了机会的画面。

branches.en: Panel and threshold are inseparable: the thing and the place it marks.
branches.cn: 门板与门槛不可分：一个是物，一个是它标出的位置。

branches.en: A doorway is both a physical entrance and the chance to go through it.
branches.cn: 门口既是实体入口，也是走进去的那次机会。

intro.en: Door is a Germanic word; English multiplies it through compounds rather than suffixes.
intro.cn: door 是日耳曼语词，英语主要靠复合而不是后缀来扩展它。

latinIntro.cn: 这一词族里没有 door 的拉丁同源词，所以拉丁条目留空。

definition_en: a student residence hall, a room inside it, or a word used before another noun for student housing
core_image: 熄灯后的走廊，一串钥匙轻轻碰在一起
scene: 熄灯后的走廊只剩脚步声，钥匙在锁孔里转了半圈。She tiptoed back to the dorm after the library closed.
sceneCN: 这里 dorm 是「学生宿舍」（第 1 个义项：学生住的宿舍楼，dormitory 的口语简称）；句意是图书馆关门后她踮着脚回到了宿舍。

pos.zh: 名词：宿舍；宿舍楼；宿舍房间

senses.title: A student residence hall
senses.definition: a building where students live during term time, the informal short form of dormitory
senses.definitionCN: 学期内学生居住的楼房，是 dormitory 的口语简称
senses.example: The dorm stands next to the sports field.
senses.exampleCN: 宿舍楼紧挨着运动场。
senses.why: Students cut the long Latin-derived dormitory down to four letters, but kept the building and its communal life in the short form.
senses.whyCN: 学生把源自拉丁语的长词 dormitory 缩成四个字母，但这一简称仍然保留了那栋楼和集体生活。

senses.title: A room in a hall
senses.definition: a single room used by a student inside a residence hall
senses.definitionCN: 宿舍楼里供一名学生使用的单个房间
senses.example: His dorm is small but has a desk by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 他的宿舍不大，但窗边有一张书桌。
senses.why: The building name slides down to the room, since students speak of the place they actually sleep in.
senses.whyCN: 楼房的名称滑落到房间上，因为学生说的是自己真正睡觉的那个地方。

senses.title: Of student housing
senses.definition: used before another noun to describe things connected with student housing
senses.definitionCN: 用在另一个名词前，描述与学生住宿有关的事物
senses.example: Dorm food is cheap but rarely exciting.
senses.exampleCN: 宿舍饭菜便宜，但很少让人惊喜。
senses.why: A place name easily becomes a label, so dorm attaches to food, life and mates as if it were an adjective.
senses.whyCN: 地名很容易变成标签，于是 dorm 像形容词一样贴到 food、life 与 mate 前面。

intro.en: Dorm is a clipped form of dormitory, from Latin dormitorium, a sleeping place.
intro.cn: dorm 是 dormitory 的缩略形式，后者来自拉丁语 dormitorium（睡觉的地方）。

items.en: Dormire meant to sleep, and it sits at the base of the whole family.
items.cn: dormire 意为「睡觉」，是整个词族的基底。

items.en: Dormitorium named a sleeping room, especially one shared by several people.
items.cn: dormitorium 指睡觉的房间，尤指多人共用的房间。

items.en: English dormitory first named a shared sleeping room in a monastery or school.
items.cn: 英语 dormitory 最初指修道院或学校里共用的睡房。

items.en: Universities expanded dormitories into large residence buildings for students.
items.cn: 大学把 dormitory 扩展成大型学生宿舍楼。

items.en: The clipped form dorm spread in student speech and in campus notices.
items.cn: 缩略形式 dorm 在学生口语与校园告示中流行起来。

items.en: Dorm now appears in compounds such as dorm room and dorm life.
items.cn: 今天 dorm 出现在 dorm room、dorm life 这类复合词中。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin sleep root; the near-meaning group names other shared housing.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「睡」的词根；近义组收的是其他集体住处。

entries.definition: The full word for a student residence or shared sleeping building.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宿舍、集体宿舍」，是 dorm 的全称。

entries.definition: A window set in a roof, from an old word for a sleeping room.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「屋顶窗」，来自旧时表示睡房的词，与 dorm 同源。

entries.definition: A rare word meaning causing sleep.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「催眠的；安眠药」，较少使用，同出 dormire。

entries.definition: A formal American term for a student dormitory building.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「学生宿舍楼」，是美式正式说法。

entries.definition: Cheap shared accommodation for travellers or students.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「旅舍、青年宿舍」，指廉价共住的住处。

entries.definition: A large building or room; at universities it can mean a residence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大厅、楼」，在大学语境里也可指宿舍楼。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real dormire family from a sleeping room to a campus building.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的 dormire 词族，从一间睡房走到校园里的宿舍楼。

normal.en: Dormire is to sleep; dormitorium is the place for it.
normal.cn: dormire 是睡觉，dormitorium 就是睡觉的地方。

normal.en: Dormitory was first a shared sleeping room, then a whole building.
normal.cn: dormitory 先是共用的睡房，后来才指整栋楼。

normal.en: Dorm is just the first syllable that students kept.
normal.cn: dorm 只是学生保留下来的第一个音节。

normal.en: Dorm life and dorm food use the place name as a label.
normal.cn: dorm life 与 dorm food 把这个地名当作标签来用。

normal.en: A dormer window and a dorm share the same sleep root.
normal.cn: dormer window（屋顶窗）与 dorm 共享同一个「睡」词根。

abstract.en: Picture a dark corridor where one key turns in a lock.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗的走廊里，一把钥匙在锁孔里转动。

abstract.en: Picture four desks pushed against one wall of a small room.
abstract.cn: 想象四张书桌挤在一间小屋的同一面墙边。

abstract.en: Picture a whole building where every window goes dark at the same minute.
abstract.cn: 想象一整栋楼，每扇窗都在同一分钟暗下去。

examples.en: The dorm is quiet during the exam week.
examples.cn: 考试周期间宿舍很安静。

examples.en: She keeps a small plant on her dorm windowsill.
examples.cn: 她在宿舍窗台上养了一小盆植物。

examples.en: Dorm life taught him to share a kitchen.
examples.cn: 宿舍生活教会他与人共用厨房。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「逗梦」——宿舍是学生一起做梦、互相逗趣的地方，dorm 就是宿舍。

root: dorm 是 dormitory 的缩略形式。dormitory 源自拉丁语 dormitorium（睡觉的地方），由 dormire（睡）加表示地点的后缀 -torium 构成。英语十五世纪先以它指修道院或学校的共用睡房，十九世纪扩展为宿舍楼，二十世纪学生口语把它截成 dorm。

sensesIntro.en: One clipped word covers the building, the single room and the label attached to student life.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个缩略词，覆盖宿舍楼、单个房间，以及贴在学生生活上的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark corridor after lights out, with keys clicking softly.
core.cn: 核心意象：熄灯后的黑暗走廊，钥匙轻碰作响。

branches.en: THE BUILDING: the first sense is the residence hall as a whole.
branches.cn: 楼宇线：第一个义项是作为整体的宿舍楼。

branches.en: THE ROOM: the second sense narrows the building to one student's room.
branches.cn: 房间线：第二个义项把整栋楼缩小到一名学生的房间。

branches.en: THE LABEL: the third sense uses the place name before other nouns.
branches.cn: 标签线：第三个义项把这个地名放到别的名词前面。

branches.en: Building and room share the name because students move between the two every day.
branches.cn: 整栋楼与单个房间共用一个名字，因为学生每天都在两者之间来回。

branches.en: The room becomes a label: dorm food is food experienced in that room.
branches.cn: 房间变成标签：dorm food 就是在那间房里吃到的饭。

intro.en: Dorm is a clipped Latin-derived stem with a place suffix -torium behind it.
intro.cn: dorm 是截短了的拉丁词干，背后带着表示地点的后缀 -torium。

latinIntro.en: Latin dormire and dormitorium are recorded; the adjective dormitorius also existed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dormire 与 dormitorium 均有记录，形容词 dormitorius 也存在。

definition_zh: 宿舍；学生宿舍楼；集体宿舍；睡城
definition_en: a building where students or workers sleep, or a residential area from which people commute to work
core_image: 清晨的走廊，一排提着洗漱袋的人往水房走
scene: 天还没亮，走廊里已经有人提着洗漱袋去排队。The new dormitory houses four hundred students.
